name: arpeggio-part
description:
Part of an arpeggio (for example 1-3, or 1-3-5) over a chord or a progression; chords cycle to fill `bars`, the
degrees repeat one per beat. `place` gives each chord a box and part; `across` connects one arpeggio from one box
part to the next. Also takes `bpm` and `repeats`.

Example: `{ "shape": "arpeggio-part", "chords": ["C","Am","F","G"], "degrees": ["1","3","5"], "bars": 4, "place": [{ "box": 1, "part": "lower" }, { "box": 1, "part": "upper" }, { "box": 2, "part": "lower" }, { "box": 2, "part": "upper" }], "bpm": 70 }`

props.name: degrees
props.description: arpeggio degrees from the chord root: ["1","3","5"]

props.name: across
props.description: cross from one box part to another: { "from": { "box": 1, "part": "upper" }, "to": { "box": 2, "part": "upper" } }

props.name: place
props.description: box and part per chord, in order

props.name: guide
props.description: cue text per step, in order

name: chord-steps
description:
Per chord, a list of steps, one beat each: "strum" or a degree. Each chord takes one bar, more when its steps need
them. Degrees are major-relative semitones from the chord root (default) or the key (when `key` is given). `guide`
gives a cue per step, in order. Also takes `bpm` and `repeats`.

Example: `{ "shape": "chord-steps", "voicing": "barre", "chords": [{ "chord": "G", "steps": ["strum","1","6","1"] }, { "chord": "D", "steps": ["strum","4","5","4"] }], "bpm": 70 }`

props.name: chords
props.type: { chord: string; steps: ("strum" | Degree)[]; place?: Place }[]
props.description: chords in order, each with its steps and optional box/part

props.name: guide
props.description: cue text per step, in order; missing ones get a default cue on a box change

name: melody
description:
A tune from the singing book, by number, in a key. Also takes `bpm` and `repeats`.

Example: `{ "shape": "melody", "tune": 3, "key": "d", "bpm": 80 }`

name: play-along
description:
Play along with a click and piano: the music shown as tab, as note names or on the neck, all following one clock.
You choose the musical content as a shape; the app computes the notes, frets, strings and timing. Shapes, by name:
`progression`, `two-scales`, `chord-steps`, `arpeggio-part`, `melody`, `solo-over` (see each shape's doc).
The student can change tempo and view, and pick a backing when the shape offers more than one.

Example: `{ "type": "play-along", "shape": { "shape": "chord-steps", "voicing": "barre", "chords": [{ "chord": "G", "steps": ["strum","1","6","1"] }, { "chord": "D", "steps": ["strum","4","5","4"] }] }, "bpm": 70, "repeats": 4 }`

props.name: shape
props.description: the musical content: one shape object, its `shape` field naming it

props.name: repeats
props.description: how many times the timeline loops (1-50); absent loops until stopped

props.name: highlight
props.description: degrees to stand out (major-relative, from the chord root): ["1","3"]

name: progression
description:
A chord progression, by chord names or by numerals in a key, cycled to fill `bars`. Optional `steps` repeat over
each chord's beats, one beat each ("strum" or a degree). Degrees are major-relative semitones ("3" is always 4),
counted from the chord root (`degreesFrom: "chord"`, default) or the key. `backing` lists comping patterns, the
first plays first. `place` gives each chord a box and part, in order. Also takes `bpm` and `repeats`.

Example: `{ "shape": "progression", "key": "g", "numerals": ["I","IV","V"], "steps": ["1","3","5"], "bars": 4, "bpm": 70, "repeats": 6 }`

props.name: numerals
props.description: I ii iii IV V vi vii°, bVII, V7 (major-key degrees; lower case = minor)

props.name: chords
props.description: chord names, used when numerals are absent: "G", "Em7"

props.name: bars
props.description: total bars; chords cycle to fill them

props.name: steps
props.description: repeated step template: "strum" or a degree like "1", "b3"

props.name: degreesFrom
props.description: what the step degrees count from: "chord" (default) or "key"

props.name: backing
props.description: comping patterns the student can pick, first one plays first

props.name: place
props.description: box and part per chord, in order: [{ "box": 1, "part": "lower" }]

name: solo-over
description:
Improvise over chords: per chord an optional scale (named from the chord root), target chord tones shown
highlighted (degrees, major-relative), and an optional `approach` hint. The code plays the backing; no fixed
notes, nothing graded. Each chord takes `bars` bars (default 1). Also takes `bpm` and `repeats`.

Example: `{ "shape": "solo-over", "key": "g", "chords": [{ "chord": "Am7", "scale": "dorian", "target": ["1","b3"] }, { "chord": "D7", "scale": "mixolydian", "target": ["3"], "approach": "land on the 3rd on beat 1" }], "bpm": 90 }`

props.name: chords
props.type: { chord: string; scale?: string; target: Degree[]; approach?: string }[]
props.description: chords in order with scale slug, target degrees and optional hint

name: two-scales
description:
Play in one scale, then switch to another at a bar (default halfway), same click throughout. Each side has its own
key. Also takes `bpm` and `repeats`.

Example: `{ "shape": "two-scales", "a": { "key": "a", "scale": "minor-pentatonic" }, "b": { "key": "a", "scale": "dorian" }, "bars": 8, "bpm": 80 }`

props.name: a
props.description: first scale: key ("a") and scale slug ("minor-pentatonic", "dorian", "major-ionian")

props.name: switchBar
props.description: bar the switch happens at (0-based), default half of bars, kept within 1..bars-1
